       What started as a demonstration in support of a teacher strike at a suburban high school almost two weeks ago has now snowballed into a series of violence as police attempt to contain what has become a national crisis. More than 6,000 people have been taken into police custody, a majority of them minors. Teachers and delegates from trade unions are now joining students on the streets to call attention to school conditions. CNN's Melissa Bell reports from Paris.

Tear gas was thrown at protesters during demonstrations in the French city of Lyon on Tuesday. Large crowds of high schoolers were out protesting in both Lyon and also the northeastern city of Strasbourg where masked youths chanted and banged on bins.

Over what started as a demonstration in support of striking teachers has now snowballed into a national crisis. French students in Paris tell CNN why they are participating in the protests that have rocked the country.
